chunks: Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah al-Zuhri narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Himyari narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ayyub, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr al-Khath'ami, from a man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) that he said:
The Qa'im (the Rising One) will not rise until twelve men have arisen, all of whom agree upon the statement that they have seen him, so they will be considered liars.

key_terms.اثْنَا عَشَرَ رَجُلًا: Twelve men, referring to a specific group of claimants
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qa'im (The Rising One), a title for the Mahdi in Shia eschatology
key_terms.يَجْمَعُونَ عَلَى قَوْلٍ: Agree upon a statement, indicating a consensus among the claimants
key_terms.يُكَذِّبُهُمْ: They are considered liars, indicating their claim is false

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of the twelve men who claim to have seen the Mahdi before his appearance?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies a specific pre-appearance sign where twelve men emerge claiming to have seen the Mahdi, only to be rejected as liars by the people. In Shia eschatology, this highlights the period of widespread confusion and the testing of faith before the true Qa'im reveals himself, distinguishing his authentic presence from false claimants. The rejection underscores the need for discernment among the believers during the era of the Minor and Major Ghaiba.
